easy.def: To hit something hard.
examples: I whack the ball.
He whacked the pole.
She whacked the weeds.

more.def: To hit something with a loud, hard blow.
examples: He whacked the ball over the fence.
She whacked the weeds with a stick.
I whacked the drum.

easy.def: A very big animal that lives in the sea.
examples: The whale swam by.
A whale is huge.
We saw a whale.

more.def: A huge sea animal that breathes air through a hole on top of its head.
examples: The whale blew water high into the air.
Blue whales are the biggest animals on Earth.
We went on a boat to watch whales.

easy.def: A word for a loud, hard hit.
examples: Wham! The door shut.
The ball hit with a wham.
Wham went the drum.

more.def: A word used for the sound of a hard, sudden hit or crash.
examples: Wham! The door slammed shut in the wind.
The ball hit the wall with a loud wham.
Wham! The bat hit the ball over the fence.

easy.def: A sudden bad event.
examples: It was a double whammy.
The storm was a whammy.
What a whammy!

more.def: A sudden blow or piece of bad luck.
examples: It was a double whammy when it rained and the car broke.
The flat tire and the rain were a whammy.
What a whammy that was.

easy.def: A place for boats to tie up.
examples: The boat was tied to the wharf.
We walked on the wharf.
The fish came to the wharf.

more.def: A flat structure built beside the water where ships tie up to load and unload.
examples: Fishing boats unloaded their catch at the wharf.
We walked along the wooden wharf at sunset.
The ship tied up to the wharf and the sailors came ashore.

easy.def: A word used to ask about something.
examples: What is your name?
What do you want to eat?
What is in the box?

more.def: A word used to ask a question about a thing or an idea, or to stand for the thing that someone is talking about.
examples: What time does the movie start?
I do not know what the answer is.
Tell me what you saw at the farm.

easy.def: Any thing at all.
examples: Eat whatever you like.
Do whatever you want.
Take whatever you need.

more.def: Anything or everything that, no matter what it is.
examples: You can paint whatever you like on the paper.
Whatever happens, we will stay together.
Pick whatever flavor you want.

easy.def: At all; used to stress that there is none.
examples: I have no idea whatsoever.
There is no food whatsoever.
He had no fear whatsoever.

more.def: At all, with no exception; used after a word like none or no.
examples: I have no idea whatsoever what the answer is.
There was no food whatsoever left in the kitchen.
She had no doubt whatsoever that her team would win.

easy.def: A plant whose seeds are ground into flour.
examples: Bread is made from wheat.
The wheat field is gold.
Farmers grow wheat.

more.def: A tall grass whose seeds are ground into flour for making bread and pasta.
examples: Bread is made from wheat flour.
The golden wheat swayed in the wind.
Farmers harvest wheat in summer.

easy.def: To get something by being sweet and coaxing.
examples: She wheedled a cookie.
He wheedled his dad.
The child wheedled.

more.def: To try to get what you want by using gentle and clever words.
examples: She wheedled an extra cookie from her grandfather.
He wheedled his way into staying up late.
The puppy wheedled a treat with its sad eyes.

easy.def: A round thing that turns.
examples: The bike has two wheels.
The wheel spins.
A car has four wheels.

more.def: A round object that turns around its center and helps things roll.
examples: A bike has two wheels.
The wheel on the wagon came loose.
The car has four wheels.

easy.def: The round thing you steer with.
examples: The driver turned the wheel.
The ship's wheel is big.
Dad holds the wheel.

more.def: A round part that a driver uses to steer a car or boat.
examples: Dad held the wheel with both hands.
The captain turned the ship's wheel.
She learned to drive by gripping the wheel.

easy.def: A one-wheeled cart that you push.
examples: Dad pushed the wheelbarrow.
The wheelbarrow is full of dirt.
I filled the wheelbarrow.

more.def: A small cart with one wheel and two handles for carrying loads.
examples: Dad pushed a wheelbarrow full of dirt.
I filled the wheelbarrow with leaves.
The gardener tipped the wheelbarrow over.

easy.def: A chair with wheels for people who cannot walk.
examples: He uses a wheelchair.
The wheelchair rolls.
The ramp is for the wheelchair.

more.def: A chair with large wheels that a person who cannot walk uses to move around.
examples: He rolls his wheelchair down the ramp.
The school has ramps for wheelchairs.
She moved her wheelchair up to the table.

easy.def: The place on a boat where the wheel is.
examples: The captain stood in the wheelhouse.
The wheelhouse is small.
We went into the wheelhouse.

more.def: The enclosed area of a boat where the wheel and controls are.
examples: The captain steered from the wheelhouse.
The wheelhouse had windows on all sides.
The deckhand brought tea to the wheelhouse.

easy.def: A bike trick where you ride on one wheel.
examples: He did a wheelie.
A wheelie is a trick.
She tried a wheelie.

more.def: A trick in which you ride a bicycle or a motorbike with the front wheel lifted off the ground.
examples: He lifted the front wheel and did a wheelie down the driveway.
It takes practice to ride a wheelie without falling.
She tried a wheelie on her bike and wobbled.

easy.def: To breathe with a whistling sound.
examples: He wheezed when he ran.
The cold made me wheeze.
The old dog wheezes.

more.def: To breathe noisily with a high whistling sound, often because of a cold or trouble breathing.
examples: He wheezed after he ran up the stairs.
The cold air made her wheeze.
The old dog wheezed as it slept.

easy.def: A baby dog or wolf.
examples: The whelp slept.
A whelp is a baby dog.
The whelps played.

more.def: A young puppy or the young of a wolf or lion.
examples: The whelp slept beside its mother.
The wolf had four whelps.
A lion whelp tumbled in the grass.

easy.def: A word used to ask at what time.
examples: When is lunch?
When do we go?
When will you come?

more.def: A word used to ask about the time that something happens.
examples: When does the library open on Saturdays?
Do you know when the next bus will arrive?
When did you lose your first tooth?

easy.def: At the time that something happens.
examples: I smile when I see you.
Call me when you are home.
When it rains, we stay in.

more.def: At the moment or during the time that something happens.
examples: The frogs start singing when the sun goes down.
Turn off the lights when you leave the room.
When I was little, I was afraid of thunder.

easy.def: Any time that.
examples: Call me whenever you want.
Whenever it rains, I stay in.
Come whenever you can.

more.def: At any time that; every time that.
examples: Call me whenever you need help.
Whenever it rains, the frogs come out.
Come over whenever you like.

easy.def: A word used to ask about a place.
examples: Where is my hat?
Where do you live?
Where did the cat go?

more.def: A word used to ask about a place, or to say the place in which something happens.
examples: Where does the river begin?
This is the spot where we found the old coin.
Do you know where the library is?

easy.def: The place where someone or something is.
examples: Her whereabouts are unknown.
The dog's whereabouts is a mystery.
Do you know his whereabouts?

more.def: The place where a person or thing is.
examples: The cat's whereabouts were unknown all day.
Do you know your friend's whereabouts?
The police searched for the boy's whereabouts.

easy.def: A word that shows how two things are different.
examples: I like cats whereas my sister likes dogs.
He is tall whereas I am short.
Summer is hot whereas winter is cold.

more.def: A word used to show that two things are different from each other.
examples: I like cats, whereas my sister likes dogs.
Summer is hot, whereas winter is cold.
The first book was short, whereas the second was very long.

easy.def: By which.
examples: A system whereby we vote.
A rule whereby all can play.
A plan whereby we share.

more.def: By which, or according to which.
examples: We use a system whereby everyone gets a turn.
The club has a rule whereby members must share.
They made a plan whereby each child brings one dish.

easy.def: In any place.
examples: Sit wherever you like.
Go wherever you want.
The dog follows me wherever I go.

more.def: In or to any place at all.
examples: Camp wherever there is flat ground.
The cat naps wherever the sun shines.
Put the box wherever it fits.

easy.def: Used to talk about two choices.
examples: I do not know whether it will rain.
Tell me whether you want juice.
She asked whether we were hungry.

more.def: Used to say that there are two choices or possibilities.
examples: I wonder whether it will snow tomorrow.
Tell me whether you want juice or milk.
She could not decide whether to go or stay.

easy.def: A word you say when you feel relieved.
examples: Whew, that was close!
Whew! It is done.
Whew, I made it.

more.def: A word you say when you feel relief, or tired from hard work.
examples: "Whew! I thought I was going to be late," said Ben.
Whew, that hill was steep!
"Whew," he said, "the test is over."

easy.def: A word used to ask about one out of a few.
examples: Which one do you want?
Which is your coat?
Which way is home?

more.def: A word used to ask or tell what one of a group is meant.
examples: Which of these books have you already read?
I could not tell which twin was Ava.
Tell me which road leads to the lake.

easy.def: Any one you like out of a group.
examples: Take whichever you want.
Whichever you pick is fine.
Choose whichever is closest.

more.def: Any one of a group that someone picks, when it does not matter which.
examples: You can have whichever of the three books you like best.
Whichever you choose, I will help you carry it.
Pick whichever is nearest and we will start the game.

easy.def: No matter which one.
examples: Whichever hat you wear, you look nice.
Take whichever seat you like.
Whichever road we take, we get there.

more.def: Used to show that it does not matter which one of a group is chosen.
examples: Whichever flavor you choose, the ice cream will taste delicious.
Whichever way you walk to the park, it takes ten minutes.
Whichever team wins, we will all clap for them.

easy.def: A quick, light smell.
examples: I caught a whiff of pizza.
A whiff of flowers.
He got a whiff of smoke.

more.def: A quick, light smell of something, or a small puff of air.
examples: I caught a whiff of fresh bread as we walked past the bakery.
A whiff of smoke drifted over from the campfire.
She got a whiff of the flowers and smiled.

easy.def: At the same time as.
examples: I sing while I walk.
Read while I cook.
She naps while it rains.

more.def: During the time that something else is happening.
examples: The audience stayed quiet while the band played.
I did my homework while my sister set the table.
Birds sing while the sun comes up.

easy.def: A short time.
examples: Stay for a while.
It was a long while ago.
Rest a while.

more.def: A period of time.
examples: It took a while for the paint to dry.
We waited for a while at the bus stop.
She has not played the piano in a long while.

easy.def: A sudden wish to do something for no reason.
examples: On a whim, we went to the park.
He bought a hat on a whim.
It was just a whim.

more.def: A sudden idea or wish to do something, which comes without careful thought.
examples: On a whim, we decided to take a different road home.
She bought a bright yellow umbrella on a whim.
It was just a whim, but the picnic turned out great.

easy.def: To cry softly in a sad way.
examples: The puppy whimpers at the door.
She whimpered when she was cold.
The baby whimpered.

more.def: To make low, soft, sad crying sounds.
examples: The puppy whimpered at the door until we let it in.
The little boy whimpered when he lost his teddy bear.
A scared kitten whimpered under the porch during the thunder.

easy.def: A soft, sad cry.
examples: I heard a whimper.
The dog gave a whimper.
A small whimper came from the box.

more.def: A low, soft, sad crying sound.
examples: The puppy let out a whimper when we left.
We heard a faint whimper coming from the closet.
With a whimper, the little girl asked for her mom.

easy.def: A playful, fun idea.
examples: The story has whimsy.
A whimsy of a hat.
She laughed with whimsy.

more.def: Playful, odd or fanciful humor or behavior.
examples: The story is full of whimsy and talking animals.
She added a bit of whimsy to the room.
The painting had a sense of whimsy.

easy.def: To complain in a high, sad voice.
examples: The child whines.
The puppy whined.
Do not whine.

more.def: To make a long, high, unhappy sound, or to complain in an annoying way.
examples: The puppy whined at the door.
The child whined about bedtime.
Please do not whine about the rain.

easy.def: The soft sound a horse makes.
examples: The horse gave a whinny.
I heard a whinny.
A whinny came from the barn.

more.def: A gentle neighing sound made by a horse.
examples: A soft whinny came from the stall.
The horse gave a whinny when it saw us.
We heard a whinny across the field.

easy.def: To make the sound of a horse.
examples: The horse will whinny.
The pony whinnied.
Horses whinny.

more.def: To make the soft, high sound of a horse.
examples: The pony whinnied when it saw the apple.
The horse whinnied and tossed its head.
We heard the mare whinny in the barn.

easy.def: Complaining in a crying voice.
examples: The whiny child cried.
She has a whiny voice.
The baby was whiny.

more.def: Complaining in a high, crying voice.
examples: The tired baby was whiny all afternoon.
He spoke in a whiny voice about the rain.
The whiny puppy wanted to go out.

easy.def: To beat cream hard until it gets fluffy.
examples: Dad will whip the cream.
She whipped the eggs.
Whip it fast.

more.def: To beat food such as cream or eggs quickly until it is light and full of air.
examples: Mom whipped the cream for the pie.
He whipped the eggs with a fork.
We whipped the cream until it was fluffy.

easy.def: To make a soft, fast, humming sound.
examples: The fan whirs.
The machine whirred.
A helicopter whirred by.

more.def: To make a continuous low, fast humming sound.
examples: The fan whirred in the corner of the room.
The machine whirred as it started up.
A helicopter whirred overhead.

easy.def: A soft, fast humming sound.
examples: I heard a whir in the room.
The whir was soft.
A whir of wings.

more.def: A low, fast humming sound made by something spinning.
examples: I heard the whir of the fan.
The whir of the bike's wheels grew louder.
A whir of wings came from the hummingbird.

easy.def: To spin around fast.
examples: The leaves whirled.
She whirled around.
Whirl the top.

more.def: To spin or turn around very fast.
examples: Leaves whirled in the wind.
She whirled around when she heard her name.
The dancers whirled across the floor.

easy.def: A fast spin.
examples: A whirl of leaves.
The dance was a whirl.
We gave it a whirl.

more.def: A fast spinning movement, or a busy time.
examples: A whirl of leaves blew past us.
The party was a whirl of music and dancing.
Let's give the new game a whirl.

easy.def: Water that spins around in a circle.
examples: The whirlpool spun.
A whirlpool is in the river.
We saw a whirlpool.

more.def: A strong current of water that spins round and round.
examples: A whirlpool swirled in the river.
Water spun around the whirlpool and down the drain.
Boaters stayed away from the whirlpool.

easy.def: A wind that spins around fast.
examples: A whirlwind blew leaves.
The whirlwind spun.
We saw a whirlwind.

more.def: A tall column of wind that whirls around fast, often carrying dust.
examples: A whirlwind picked up the leaves and spun them.
Dust swirled in a small whirlwind on the road.
The visit was a whirlwind of fun, with no time to rest.

easy.def: To mix quickly with a tool.
examples: Whisk the eggs.
Mom whisked the cream.
I whisk the batter.

more.def: To beat or mix food quickly, or to move something away fast.
examples: Whisk the eggs until they are fluffy.
Mom whisked the cream until it was thick.
The waiter whisked the plates away.

easy.def: A tool for beating eggs or cream.
examples: Mom used a whisk.
The whisk is metal.
I held the whisk.

more.def: A kitchen tool made of wire loops, used to beat eggs or cream.
examples: Mom beat the eggs with a whisk.
The whisk was covered in cream.
He stirred the batter with a whisk.

easy.def: A long, stiff hair on a cat's face.
examples: The cat has long whiskers.
A whisker is stiff.
The mouse has whiskers.

more.def: One of the long, stiff hairs that grow near the mouth of a cat or other animal.
examples: The cat's whiskers twitched.
A mouse uses its whiskers to feel its way.
The dog had a few gray whiskers.

easy.def: The long, stiff hairs near a cat's nose.
examples: The cat has whiskers.
Her whiskers twitched.
The mouse has whiskers.

more.def: The long, stiff hairs that grow near the nose and mouth of a cat, a mouse or another animal, which help it feel things.
examples: The cat's whiskers twitched when it smelled the fish.
Whiskers help a cat feel its way in the dark.
The mouse sniffed the air with its tiny whiskers.

easy.def: To talk in a very soft voice.
examples: Whisper so you do not wake the baby.
She whispered in my ear.
We whisper in the library.

more.def: To speak very softly, using your breath instead of your full voice.
examples: He whispered the secret into his sister's ear.
The children whispered so they would not wake the baby.
The wind whispered through the tall grass.

easy.def: To make a high sound by blowing air through your lips.
examples: I can whistle.
She whistled a tune.
He whistles when he walks.

more.def: To make a high, clear sound by blowing air through your lips or a small tool.
examples: She whistled a happy tune on her way to school.
The wind whistled through the trees.
The referee whistled to stop the game.

easy.def: A small tool that makes a loud, high sound.
examples: The coach blew a whistle.
The whistle is loud.
I heard a whistle.

more.def: A small tube that makes a loud, high sound when you blow into it.
examples: The coach blew her whistle at the end of practice.
A train whistle sounded in the distance.
The referee's whistle stopped the game.

easy.def: Having the color of snow.
examples: Snow is white.
She wore a white shirt.
Milk is white.

more.def: Having the color of fresh snow or milk.
examples: The white clouds floated across the blue sky.
A polar bear's white fur helps it hide in the snow.
The baker wore a clean white apron.

easy.def: The color of snow.
examples: White is my favorite color.
I mixed some white into the red paint.
Doctors often dress in white.

more.def: The color of fresh snow; it is the lightest color there is.
examples: The artist added a little white to make the paint lighter.
The mountain peaks were covered in a blanket of white.
Dressed all in white, the team stood out against the green field.

easy.def: To make or become white.
examples: Snow whitened the hills.
Her hair whitened.
The paint whitens the wall.

more.def: To make something white, or to become white.
examples: Snow whitened the hills overnight.
His hair slowly whitened with age.
Bleach whitened the old shirt.

easy.def: White paint for fences and walls.
examples: The fence has whitewash.
Whitewash is white.
A bucket of whitewash.

more.def: A cheap white paint made of lime and water, used on fences and walls.
examples: Tom Sawyer had to paint the fence with whitewash.
A bucket of whitewash sat by the barn.
The walls were covered with whitewash.

easy.def: To paint with white paint.
examples: Whitewash the fence.
They whitewashed the wall.
He will whitewash the barn.

more.def: To cover a surface with white paint made of lime and water.
examples: They whitewashed the walls of the old barn.
He whitewashed the fence on Saturday.
Whitewash the stones around the garden.

easy.def: A little white.
examples: The sky was whitish.
A whitish powder.
The whitish stone.

more.def: Somewhat white; close to white.
examples: The sky looked whitish before the snow.
A whitish powder covered the table.
The whitish stone sparkled.

easy.def: To cut small bits off wood to shape it.
examples: Grandpa will whittle a stick.
He whittled a duck.
She whittled a spoon.

more.def: To shape wood by cutting small pieces off with a knife.
examples: Grandpa whittled a duck from a block of wood.
She whittled a stick into a spoon.
He whittled the branch down to a point.

easy.def: To move by very fast with a buzzing sound.
examples: A bike whizzed past me.
The ball whizzed by.
Cars whiz down the road.

more.def: To move quickly through the air with a humming or buzzing sound.
examples: A bee whizzed past my ear and landed on a flower.
The ball whizzed over the net and into the grass.
Cars whizzed by on the highway as we waited at the crossing.

easy.def: A person who is very good at something.
examples: She is a math whiz.
My brother is a computer whiz.
Our teacher is a whiz at spelling.

more.def: A person who is very clever or skilled at doing something.
examples: She is a whiz at solving puzzles.
He is a computer whiz and fixed our printer in a minute.
The new student turned out to be a whiz at chess.

easy.def: A word used to ask which person.
examples: Who is at the door?
Who has my hat?
Who wants some juice?

more.def: A word used to ask which person or people, or to tell more about a person you just named.
examples: Who wrote the book about the sea turtle?
The girl who sits next to me is new.
I know who left the muddy footprints on the floor.

easy.def: A word that means stop.
examples: Whoa, slow down!
Whoa, look at that!
The rider said whoa.

more.def: A word you say to make a horse stop, or to show surprise.
examples: Whoa, the roller coaster is huge!
The rider called whoa and the horse stopped.
Whoa, that is a big wave!

easy.def: Any person who.
examples: Whoever wants a turn can come.
Take whoever you like.
Whoever finds it wins.

more.def: Any person at all who; it does not matter which person.
examples: Whoever finishes first gets a prize.
Give the book to whoever asks for it.
Whoever left the door open, please close it.

easy.def: All of something, with no part missing.
examples: I ate the whole apple.
She read the whole book.
The whole class cheered.

more.def: Complete, with nothing left out or broken.
examples: He ate the whole sandwich and was still hungry.
The whole class went on the trip to the zoo.
We looked for the whole afternoon but could not find the key.

easy.def: Good for your body and mind.
examples: A wholesome meal.
Wholesome fun.
Wholesome food.

more.def: Good for your health, or good in a clean and kind way.
examples: Mom made a wholesome meal of vegetables and rice.
We had a wholesome afternoon playing outside.
The show was wholesome and full of kindness.

easy.def: All the way, completely.
examples: I am wholly sure.
The dish was wholly gone.
He is wholly happy.

more.def: Completely, in every way.
examples: I am wholly sure that I locked the door.
The story is wholly made up.
She was wholly focused on her book.

easy.def: Which person.
examples: To whom did you give it?
Whom did you see?
With whom are you going?

more.def: Used to ask or tell which person is the object of an action.
examples: To whom should I give this note?
Whom did you invite to the party?
She is the girl with whom I work.

easy.def: To shout loudly with joy.
examples: The kids whooped.
We whoop for joy.
They whooped and cheered.

more.def: To give a loud cry of joy or excitement.
examples: The kids whooped when the bell rang.
We whooped for joy when we won.
She whooped and threw her hat in the air.

easy.def: A rushing sound.
examples: The wind made a whoosh.
I heard a whoosh.
The train went whoosh.

more.def: A soft, rushing sound like air moving fast.
examples: The ball flew by with a whoosh.
I heard a whoosh of wind.
The train zoomed past with a whoosh.

easy.def: Something very big, or a big lie.
examples: He caught a whopper of a fish.
That is a whopper of a pumpkin.
She told a whopper.

more.def: Something very large, or a story that is a big exaggeration.
examples: He caught a whopper of a fish at the lake.
The farmer grew a whopper of a pumpkin.
His tale of seeing a giant bird was a whopper.

easy.def: Very big.
examples: A whopping fish.
The whopping pizza.
A whopping bill.

more.def: Very large, often used for fun.
examples: He caught a whopping fish.
We ate a whopping big pizza.
The whopping pile of snow blocked the door.

easy.def: A curl shape.
examples: The shell has a whorl.
A whorl of hair.
The fingerprint has whorls.

more.def: A shape that spirals around a center, like the lines on a fingertip or a shell.
examples: The snail's shell had a perfect whorl.
A whorl of hair stuck up on his head.
Fingerprints have loops and whorls.

easy.def: A word used to ask for the reason.
examples: Why is the sky blue?
Why are you sad?
Why did the bell ring?

more.def: A word used to ask for the reason that something happens or is done.
examples: Why do leaves change color in the fall?
I do not know why my pencil keeps breaking.
Can you explain why we need to sleep?
